status.label: Fix plan ready for design
status.detail: Identity lookup and startup placement are concrete restore boundaries.

next_action.label: Design fix
next_action.reason: Classify failures by app identity and placement timing.

judgment.rationale: Several applications are named and the issue includes a diagnostic archive. Current code retrieves last-zone history using the new window plus work-area/layout identity, which is a concrete path for app identity and creation-timing failures.
evidence: PowerToys Settings, Teams, cmd.exe, Total Commander, Windows Terminal, and Notion were reported not to restore.
Current FancyZones::MoveToAppLastZone calls GetAppLastZoneIndexSet(window, work-area identity, layout id) and snaps only when a matching history entry is found.
Related #23003 concerned per-app control, not the underlying missed restore.
judgment.recommended_action: Reproduce with representative app models and harden application identity/timing before designing broad allow/block behavior.

fix_assessment.rationale: No existing fix covers the cross-application history lookup and startup-placement failure.

proposed_fixes.title: Make last-zone restore resilient to app identity and startup placement timing
proposed_fixes.root_cause: Some applications create replacement/top-level windows whose executable, AUMID, owner, or final bounds differ from the window recorded in app-zone history, or they apply their own placement after FancyZones restores the zone.
plan: Trace history key creation and lookup for classic Win32, packaged, Electron, and console-hosted apps.
Use a stable application identity with documented fallback rules and defer the snap until the eligible final top-level window is ready.
Avoid repeated fighting with applications that intentionally reposition themselves, and retain exclusion rules.
verification: Add unit tests for history lookup across HWND recreation and stable app identity.
Launch Windows Terminal, Notion, and a simple Win32 control after zoning, then verify only previously zoned eligible windows restore.
Test multi-monitor, virtual-desktop, and layout-change behavior.

confidence.rationale: The lookup path and app-dependent symptom are clear, but identity mismatch versus post-launch self-positioning must be measured per app.

issue_context.summary: FancyZones last-zone restore works inconsistently across applications because restoration depends on matching a newly created HWND to saved application history and acting before or after the application’s own placement logic.
known_information: Multiple unrelated application frameworks fail to return to their last zone.
The setting is enabled and manual Shift-drag records a zone.
Current restore requires both matching app history and matching work-area/layout identity.
inferences: Failures may divide into history-key misses and applications overriding placement after FancyZones snaps.
issue_context.analysis: The cross-app list argues against one app bug, while current code exposes two testable boundaries: identity lookup and snap timing.

reproduce.title: Classify FancyZones restore failures
prerequisites: Enable “Move newly created windows to their last known zone”
Install representative apps such as Windows Terminal and Notion
steps: Zone each test app and confirm app-zone-history records it.
Close the app completely and relaunch it.
Capture the new HWND, executable/AUMID, owner, initial bounds, and bounds after startup settles.
Compare a simple Win32 app that restores correctly.
reproduce.expected_result: Each eligible app is matched to its saved history and remains in the restored zone after its startup placement completes.
